content: Cimetidine interacts with a wide range of medications by altering their metabolism, absorption, or clearance, primarily through its effects on hepatic and intestinal enzymes (e.g., CYP450 enzymes) and transporters (e.g., P-glycoprotein). Below is a detailed explanation of its interactions with specific drugs: 1. Cimetidine and Tafenoquine: Tafenoquine inhibits organic cation transporter-2 (OCT2) and multidrug and toxin extrusion (MATE) transporters. Co-administration with OCT2 or MATE substrates should be avoided. If unavoidable, monitor for substrate-related toxicities and consider dosage adjustments based on the co-administered drug's labeling. 2. Cimetidine and Tapentadol: Cimetidine increases tapentadol's effects by reducing its metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 3. Cimetidine and Temsirolimus: Cimetidine increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Cimetidine and Tepotinib: Tepotinib increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter. Avoid this combination or reduce the P-gp substrate dosage if recommended in the product labeling. 5. Cimetidine and Theophylline: Cimetidine increases theophylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6. Cimetidine and Thioridazine: Cimetidine increases thioridazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Cimetidine and Tipranavir: Cimetidine increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 8. Cimetidine and Tizanidine: Cimetidine increases tizanidine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 9. Cimetidine and Tofacitinib: Cimetidine increases tofacitinib levels by reducing its metabolism. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg daily when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 10. Cimetidine and Tolterodine: Cimetidine increases tolterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Cimetidine and Tolvaptan: Cimetidine increases tolvaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 12. Cimetidine and Triamcinolone Acetonide Injectable Suspension: Cimetidine increases triamcinolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Cimetidine and Triazolam: Cimetidine increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 14. Cimetidine and Trilaciclib: Trilaciclib decreases cimetidine levels by inhibiting OCT2, MATE1, and MATE-2K transporters. Avoid co-administration with substrates where even minimal concentration increases may lead to serious toxicities. 15. Cimetidine and Verapamil: Cimetidine increases verapamil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Cimetidine and Vilazodone: Cimetidine increases vilazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If intolerable adverse effects occur, reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily. 17. Cimetidine and Warfarin: Cimetidine increases warfarin's effects through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Cimetidine and Acalabrutinib: Cimetidine decreases acalabrutinib levels by increasing gastric pH, which reduces acalabrutinib solubility. This interaction applies only to oral forms. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 19. Cimetidine and Alfentanil: Cimetidine increases alfentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Cimetidine and Alosetron: Cimetidine increases alosetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Cimetidine and Amitriptyline: Cimetidine increases amitriptyline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Cimetidine and Apalutamide: Apalutamide decreases cimetidine levels by increasing its elimination. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Cimetidine and Armodafinil: Cimetidine increases armodafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Cimetidine and Atazanavir: Cimetidine increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Cimetidine and Atogepant: Cimetidine increases atogepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Cimetidine and Atomoxetine: Cimetidine increases atomoxetine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Cimetidine and Avanafil: Cimetidine increases avanafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the maximum avanafil dose to 50 mg once every 24 hours when co-administered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 28. Cimetidine and Avapritinib: Cimetidine increases avapritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Cimetidine and Azelastine: Cimetidine increases azelastine levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Cimetidine and Bendamustine: Cimetidine increases bendamustine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism, potentially reducing the formation of active metabolites. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Cimetidine and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Cimetidine increases hydrocodone levels (a metabolite of benzhydrocodone) by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Cimetidine and Berotralstat: Berotralstat increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein transporters. Monitor or titrate the P-gp substrate dose if co-administered. 33. Cimetidine and Bexarotene: Cimetidine increases bexarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Cimetidine and Bortezomib: Cimetidine increases bortezomib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Cimetidine and Bosentan: Cimetidine increases bosentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Cimetidine and Bosutinib: Bosutinib increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Cimetidine and Brexpiprazole: Cimetidine increases brexpiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose if co-administered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor. 38. Cimetidine and Budesonide: Cimetidine decreases budesonide levels by increasing gastric pH, which may cause premature dissolution of extended-release tablets. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 39. Cimetidine and Cabazitaxel: Cimetidine increases cabazitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Cimetidine and Cabozantinib: Cimetidine increases cabozantinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Cimetidine and Carbamazepine: Cimetidine increases carbamazepine levels by reducing its metabolism. Monitor plasma levels closely when used concomitantly. 42. Cimetidine and Carbonyl Iron: Cimetidine decreases carbonyl iron levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing its solubility. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cimetidine and Carvedilol: Cimetidine increases carvedilol levels by inhibiting CYP2C9/10 and CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Cimetidine and Cefdinir: Cimetidine decreases cefdinir levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Cimetidine and Cefditoren: Cimetidine decreases cefditoren levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Cimetidine and Cefpodoxime: Cimetidine decreases cefpodoxime levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Cimetidine and Cefuroxime: Cimetidine decreases cefuroxime levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Cimetidine and Cevimeline: Cimetidine increases cevimeline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Cimetidine and Chlordiazepoxide: Cimetidine increases chlordiazepoxide levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Cimetidine and Cilostazol: Cimetidine increases cilostazol toxicity by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Consider reducing the cilostazol dose. 51. Cimetidine and Citalopram: Cimetidine increases citalopram levels by inhibiting CYP2C19 metabolism. Limit the maximum citalopram dose to 20 mg/day to reduce the risk of QT prolongation. 52. Cimetidine and Clarithromycin: Cimetidine increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clarithromycin also increases cimetidine levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Cimetidine and Clomipramine: Cimetidine increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Cimetidine and Clonazepam: Cimetidine increases clonazepam levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Cimetidine and Clopidogrel: Cimetidine reduces clopidogrel's efficacy by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which is required for clopidogrel's activation. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Cimetidine and Clorazepate: Cimetidine increases clorazepate levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Cimetidine and Clozapine: Cimetidine increases clozapine levels by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Cimetidine and Codeine: Cimetidine prevents the conversion of codeine to its active metabolite morphine by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Cimetidine and Conivaptan: Cimetidine increases conivaptan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Cimetidine and Crizotinib: Cimetidine decreases crizotinib levels by increasing gastric pH, reducing its solubility. Use caution and monitor closely. This list is extensive but not exhaustive. For each interaction, it is critical to assess the clinical significance and adjust therapy accordingly.
